claim: In the matching retail DLL, FormAnimator.PreprocessEachAnm (0x06004E78) is a parameterless 1,149-byte method. It resolves this.plObj.TargetPlIdx through PlayerMan.GetPlObj, reads this.CurrentSkill.anmData[this.CurrentAnmIdx].anmStartState, subtracts one, and dispatches through a 20-target switch for numeric values 1 through 20; other values go directly to return. The exact case effects are pinned in the provenance summary: sixteen cases call Player.ChangeState using literals 22, 34, 35, 36, or 38; selected cases also clear penaltyTime, set grappleType, or reverse target/host PlDir; the remaining cases perform the exact ring/PostPos bookkeeping, AddBP(-12288f), standing-stun/down-time initialization, ChangeRefereeGiveUpAnm store, or Poisoned call recorded there. Matching-DLL StartAnm has exactly one method call, to PreprocessEachAnm. CAP-R6-001 does not trace PreprocessEachAnm as its own event, but among 5,333 StartAnm executions it contains exactly two direct nested Player.ChangeState records, at raw line quartets 96086-96089 and 321684-321687. Both raw children carry argument string Grapple and change the recorded StartAnm state from NormalAnm to Grapple. The capture does not expose anmStartState, so neither observation is assigned to a numeric switch case.
